data.title: Intuit Stock (INTU) Plunges on $3.68B Mailchimp Sale to Bending Spoons and Weak Guidance
data.description:
Intuit (INTU) stock plunged in Friday's pre-market trading after the tax software company announced the sale of its marketing subsidiary Mailchimp to Italian technology conglomerate Bending Spoons (BSP) in a $3.68 billion deal. The acquisition is expected to be completed in early 2027. Intuit investors were disappointed as the deal price is less than one-third of the $12 billion the company paid to buy Mailchimp in 2021. Weak guidance also weighed on investor sentiment on Intuit shares.

Latest Earnings of Intuit and Bending Spoons

Intuit's full-year guidance overshadowed its better-than-expected earnings and revenue for the first quarter of Fiscal 2027. The company's revenue grew 12% to $4.35 billion in Q1 FY27. However, Mailchimp revenue declined 1% to $313 million. Management expects FY27 adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $22.88 to $23.12 and revenue of $23.081 billion to $23.365 billion. Analysts expected adjusted EPS of $23.62 on revenue of $23.43 billion. Intuit expects Mailchimp's FY27 revenue in the range of $1.256 billion to $1.266 billion, down 1% to flat year-over-year.

Intuit blamed its underwhelming outlook on a shift in its personal-finance platform, Credit Karma, which is under pressure due to ⁠higher interest rates, and a faster-than-expected change in consumer behavior toward its business.

Meanwhile, Bending Spoons announced better-than-expected Q3 results, with revenue rising 125% year-over-year to $780 million, mainly driven by acquisitions. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS) surged 98% to $0.42.

Rationale Behind the Mailchimp Deal and Financial Terms

Bending Spoons is acquiring Mailchimp, the email marketing automation platform for businesses, for $3.31 billion in cash and $368 million in BSP stock. Luca Ferrari, Bending Spoons' CEO, said that the company will make significant investments in Mailchimp, "building on the powerful, easy-to-use tools customers already value and rely on."

The deal has been approved by Bending Spoons' board. The company added that it will acquire Mailchimp by purchasing 100% of The Rocket Science Group, LLC, along with other assets and liabilities of the Mailchimp business. Notably, Bending Spoons, which ​went public in July, continues to enhance its portfolio with another major digital business. It bought productivity software startup Airtable in September.

Bending Spoons' portfolio also comprises AOL, Brightcove, Eventbrite, and WeTransfer, among other brands. Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B) invested $600 million in Bending Spoons when the company went public in July. In October, Bending Spoons said Berkshire invested an additional $330 million.

For Intuit, the Mailchimp sale aligns with its strategy to focus on AI-powered products for small businesses. Intuit had acquired Mailchimp as part of its efforts to expand beyond the core tax and accounting businesses. The company plans ​to use the cash proceeds from the deal to repurchase shares.

Wall Street's Take on BSP and INTU Stocks

According to TipRanks' Stock Comparison Tool, Wall Street has a Moderate Buy consensus rating on both Bending Spoons and Intuit. The average price targets indicate 21.5% upside potential in INTU stock, while BSP is expected to rise 8.4%.

However, these ratings and price targets are expected to change as analysts react to the Mailchimp deal and latest results.

data.title: Apple's New AI Agent Could Put It Up Against OpenAI, Meta, and Anthropic
data.description:
Apple (AAPL) is reportedly developing its own AI agent that can perform tasks for users. According to Bloomberg, Apple has revealed its plans through new job listings. This would put the company in a fast-growing AI agent market where OpenAI, Anthropic (ANT), Meta (META), and others are already working on similar tools.

What Tasks Will Apple's AI Agent Handle?

The report stated that Apple's AI agent will be able to browse the web, use apps, control devices, and write code for users.

The company's new job openings posted on its website this week gave a clear indication. One of the roles listed is for a senior engineering manager who will lead the development of a new AI assistant. The job listing says the AI agent will work across different apps and services. It will be able to visit websites, run commands, write and fix code, and control devices.

The job listing said "People already do their most valuable work by moving fluidly between tools: a browser, a document, a terminal, an editor, a service. We're building AI agents that can do the same."

Apple Joins the Race to Build AI Agents

Apple is not alone in developing AI agents. Meta's Muse has drawn strong interest in recent months by helping users book restaurant tables, plan trips, and prepare news updates. It has climbed to the No. 2 spot among free apps on Apple's App Store, behind TikTok.

Anthropic has also recently expanded testing of its AI agent, Duet. OpenAI has also added more features to Dots. Meanwhile, Google (GOOGL) updated its AI agent, now called Tasks, earlier this week.

As per the report, Apple could launch its AI agent as early as the end of next year. However, the project is still in its early stages. The company has not confirmed a launch date.

Following Apple's news, Meta shares fell 1.4% in after-hours trading on Thursday, while Anthropic shares dropped 4.7%.

Is AAPL Stock a Buy?

Apple stock has a consensus Moderate Buy rating based on 15 Buys, eight Holds, and six Sells issued in the last three months. The average AAPL price target of $343.69 implies a 1.6% downside from current levels.

data.title: Anthropic IPO Fails to Lift Market Sentiment
data.description:
U.S. stock futures traded lower ahead of Friday's market open following one of Wall Street's weakest sessions in recent months. Despite Anthropic's (ANT) blockbuster IPO, which valued the Claude AI maker at roughly $1.8 trillion, investor concerns over AI valuations and the broader technology sector remained high.

Futures on the Nasdaq-100 (NDX), the S&P 500 Index (SPX), and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) were down 1.10%, 0.51%, and 0.23%, respectively, as of 1:37 a.m. EST on November 20.

Oil prices rose in Asian trading on Friday but remained on track for a weekly decline. Concerns over supply disruptions increased after Houthi rebels launched missile attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh. Meanwhile, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, causing explosions and fires.

At the time of writing, Brent crude futures, the international benchmark, rose 0.10% to $92.07 per barrel, while WTI crude futures were up 0.19% at $83.37 per barrel.

During Thursday's regular trading session, major U.S. stock indexes fell more than 2% each, with the Dow Jones closing below 50,000 for the first time since June. The sell-off came despite an initially positive session, during which the Nasdaq gained as much as 2.1% and the S&P 500 rose 1.3%. However, stocks reversed course shortly after Anthropic began trading.

The Dow is down 6.2% this week, putting it on track for its worst weekly decline since April 2025. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq have each fallen 5%, heading for their biggest weekly losses in more than a year.

Looking ahead, investors will focus on the final reading of the University of Michigan's November consumer sentiment report. They will also monitor earnings reports from BJ's Wholesale (BJ) and WeRide (WRD).

data.title: Nvidia Stock (NVDA) Faces New Probe as Cathie Wood Sells More Shares
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) is facing another setback as questions about its former CEO Jensen Huang and China ties draw fresh scrutiny. California Attorney General Rob Bonta has now issued an investigative subpoena to the chipmaker. The move comes as Cathie Wood 's ARK Invest continues to cut its Nvidia holdings. On Thursday, the fund sold another 33,430 shares worth about $5 million.

The latest sale adds to a much larger Nvidia exit earlier this week. On November 16, ARK sold 543,092 shares worth about $84.8 million.

California AG Seeks Answers on Nvidia's China Exposure

Bonta said his office served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia on Thursday. The probe will examine whether the company or Huang helped China obtain advanced chips or confidential information.

It will also look at whether Nvidia misled investors and the public about these risks. Bonta said the conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raised "bright red flags."

The investigation follows reports about Huang's alleged relationship with Alice Huang. She is a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed. U.S. intelligence agencies are examining her possible ties to China's Ministry of State Security.

Megaspeed has also faced scrutiny over concerns it helped China gain access to Nvidia's advanced AI chips. These chips are subject to U.S. export controls. However, the allegations have not been proven, and Huang has not been accused of criminal wrongdoing.

The California probe adds to the scrutiny Nvidia already faces. The SEC is reportedly investigating whether the company misled investors. Huang is expected to testify before three House committees on December 1.

Nvidia Stock Extend Losses

Nvidia shares fell another 3.3% on Thursday, extending their losing streak to six sessions. The stock is now about 38% below its October peak. The decline has wiped out roughly $669 billion in market value over six sessions.

The latest losses came after Moody's lowered Nvidia's credit outlook from Positive to Stable. The ratings agency kept its Aa1 credit rating unchanged. However, it cited Jensen Huang's sudden exit and the lack of a formal succession plan. Moody's said Huang's departure has created uncertainty around Nvidia's business strategy and financial policies.

Nvidia's strong results have done little to calm investors. The company reported Q3 revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year-over-year. It also forecast fourth-quarter revenue of about $130 billion.

Is NVDA Stock a Buy?

Nvidia's stock has a consensus Moderate Buy rating based on 30 Buys, 13 Holds, and one Sell issued in the past three months. The average NVDA price target of $232.59 implies 59% upside from current levels.

data.title: Nvidia Nears $500M Deal for AI Startup Inception to Strengthen AI Models
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) is in advanced talks to acquire Inception for more than $500 million, a startup developing diffusion-based large language models (LLMs), according to a report by The Information. The proposed deal would give Nvidia access to new AI research talent and technology as it expands its work on AI models and robotics.

Deal Could Bring Inception's Founders to Nvidia

The proposed deal may include additional earnout payments for Inception employees, tied to specific performance targets. All three co-founders are expected to join Nvidia as part of the transaction.

The founders are Stefano Ermon, CEO of Inception and a Stanford professor; Aditya Grover, a professor at UCLA; and Volodymyr Kuleshov, a professor at Cornell University.

Founded two years ago, Inception is based in the San Francisco Bay Area and has more than 30 employees. The startup has raised $50 million from investors including Menlo Ventures, M12, Mayfield, and Nvidia.

Nvidia's talks with Inception began before the reported departure of CEO Jensen Huang. The report also noted that Microsoft (MSFT) had shown interest in a similar deal.

What Makes Inception's Technology Different?

Inception develops diffusion-based LLMs that use a different method to generate text than traditional language models.

Conventional LLMs generate text one token at a time, in sequential order. Inception's technology uses an iterative process to refine a response, allowing multiple tokens to be generated in parallel.

Its Mercury family of models is built on this approach. Inception says its models can generate text up to 10 times faster than comparable models. The company has also developed diffusion-based coding models and published research on multimodal understanding and reasoning.

Deal Could Strengthen Nvidia's Nemotron Model

The acquisition could strengthen Nvidia's efforts to develop its own AI models and expand its Nemotron portfolio of open models. Businesses and government agencies can customize these models for specific applications.

Nemotron models are already used by Booz Allen Hamilton (BAH), Palantir Technologies (PLTR), and several U.S. government agencies.

Inception's research team is also expected to explore the use of diffusion technology in physical AI models for robotics. This could support Nvidia's efforts to expand AI applications beyond language models and data centers.

Is Nvidia a Strong Buy?

On TipRanks, NVDA has a Moderate Buy consensus rating based on 30 Buys, 13 Holds, and one Sell rating. The average Nvidia price target of $232.59 implies 59.3% upside potential from current levels.

data.title: Why Nvidia Stock Extends Losses Overnight — and Why Top Investor Says "Hold Your Horses"
data.description:
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) is seeing some additional selling overnight, with shares down 1.5% following Thursday's 3.3% loss. While the chip giant continues dealing with the fallout from former CEO Jensen Huang's scandal, the latest weakness coincides with disappointing trading in Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT). The Claude developer is down around 6% in overnight trading following its record-breaking IPO, suggesting the market is approaching AI investments with caution.

But why should Anthropic's performance matter to Nvidia, beyond the broader concerns surrounding AI valuations? For starters, Nvidia is one of the Claude developer's biggest new investors, having committed $10 billion to purchase shares at the IPO price through a concurrent private placement. The two companies also have close commercial relationships, with Anthropic relying on Nvidia's technology to support its computing infrastructure. More importantly, the record-breaking debut was expected to restore confidence in the sector following weeks of selling. However, the newly listed stock gave back much of its initial gains on Thursday.

Against this backdrop, top investor James Foord, who ranks among the top 5% of stock pros on TipRanks, believes Nvidia investors should resist the temptation to rush into buying shares on the dip. Despite strong quarterly results and an attractive valuation, Foord recently downgraded NVDA to Hold, arguing that several unresolved issues deserve closer examination before committing additional money.

Nvidia certainly delivered encouraging financial results, with fiscal third-quarter revenue reaching $115.8 billion, representing 103% annual growth. The company also projected $130 billion in fourth-quarter sales, exceeding Wall Street's expectations and demonstrating continued demand for its technology. Yet, those figures haven't been enough to convince investors that the worst is over.

One of Foord's main concerns involves Nvidia's growing financial obligations, which he believes could pose risks if customer demand weakens. The company's guarantees reached $118 billion, while purchase commitments climbed to around $390 billion, raising concerns about its exposure should data center spending slow.

Another issue involves Nvidia's upcoming 10-Q filing, which will provide a more complete picture of its financial position. Unlike previous quarters, the document wasn't released alongside earnings, although the December 4 regulatory deadline has not yet passed.

"I don't think that's a reason to panic, but I do think it's a reason to wait. While I still view this as a good stock, I'm downgrading NVDA to a Hold simply due to the current uncertainty and overall market sentiment," Foord said.

The investor wants greater transparency into financing arrangements, customer payment terms, and regional sales exposure before reconsidering his recommendation. His concerns also extend to regulatory investigations and leadership changes, which have complicated the outlook despite Nvidia's continued technological strength.

Accounts receivable rose from $63.1 billion to $81 billion during the quarter, prompting Foord to seek further details about collection periods. Inventory also increased faster than sales, while unanswered issues surrounding potential shipments to China through intermediaries remain another source of concern.

Nevertheless, Foord sees little justification for existing holders to sell at current prices, given Nvidia's long-term earnings potential. Those considering an initial investment or adding to their positions, however, may benefit from waiting until the forthcoming disclosures offer greater clarity.

"Nvidia looks attractively priced, and it's hard to see how, in the long term, it will be a bad investment. For now, we hold NVDA and reassess after the filing," Foord summed up. (See NVDA stock forecast)

data.title: ANT, NVDA – Cathie Wood Buys $91M in Anthropic, Sells Nvidia Shares
data.description:
Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) made history on Thursday, but Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and the broader market had little reason to celebrate. Despite Anthropic's record-breaking IPO, Wall Street suffered another steep sell-off, with the S&P 500 plunging 2%. The Claude developer finished its first trading session 17% above its offering price, but well below its opening level. And the selling isn't over yet, with Anthropic shares slipping nearly 5% in overnight trading.

Meanwhile, Nvidia shares continue heading south, losing another 3.3% on Thursday and now sitting about 38% below their October peak, as investors struggle to regain confidence following Jensen Huang's departure and growing uncertainty surrounding the AI industry's spending commitments.

Against this backdrop, Cathie Wood is making a sizable bet on Wall Street's newest AI heavyweight while reducing her exposure to Nvidia. On Thursday, the ARK Invest founder purchased 934,968 Anthropic shares through her funds, worth about $91 million at current prices. At the same time, Wood sold 33,430 Nvidia shares valued at $4.9 million.

Anthropic Stock: Wall Street Sees More Room to Run

Anthropic's arrival on Nasdaq was anything but ordinary, with the company raising a record $81.3 billion after pricing its offering at $83 per share, surpassing SpaceX's previous IPO record. Shares opened at $111.50, briefly lifting the company's fully diluted valuation above $2 trillion, before retreating to finish Thursday at $97.17.

Yet, the company's financial commitments present a serious challenge, particularly as competition among leading AI developers continues growing. Anthropic has outlined nearly $900 billion in computing and infrastructure commitments over the coming years, raising concerns about how long it could take for revenues to justify those expenditures. Competition from OpenAI and Google adds another hurdle, especially as the cost of developing and running advanced AI models remains high.

Still, demand for Anthropic shares has been strong among institutional investors, including those outside the US. According to Reuters, Japanese investors sought about $9.4 billion worth of shares in the offering.

Wall Street remains bullish on Anthropic's prospects following its historic Nasdaq debut this week. ANT has a Strong Buy consensus rating, based on 6 Buy recommendations and one Hold assigned this week. The average 12-month price target stands at $133.33, suggesting about 37% upside from Thursday's closing price. (See ANT stock forecast)

Nvidia Stock Keeps Falling, but Wall Street Sees 60% Upside

For Nvidia, the latest earnings report offered another reminder that its operations remain strong, even as investors continue questioning the company's future leadership. The company reported quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion, representing 103% growth from the previous year, while data-center sales climbed 110% to $107.6 billion.

Nvidia also confirmed that its next-generation Vera Rubin platform has started shipping, marking another important milestone in its efforts to maintain technological leadership. Looking ahead, the company expects fourth-quarter revenue of ~$130 billion, suggesting that demand for advanced computing hardware remains robust despite growing concerns about AI infrastructure spending.

Nevertheless, investors have found little reassurance in those figures following Huang's resignation last week. Interim CEO Colette Kress is overseeing operations while Nvidia searches for a permanent successor, and the board has ruled out bringing Huang back. Meanwhile, uncertainty surrounding an ongoing investigation, the company's exposure to China, and extensive infrastructure commitments continues weighing on sentiment.

Adding to the concerns, Moody's recently revised Nvidia's credit outlook from positive to stable, giving investors another reason to reconsider the risks surrounding the company. Thursday's losses extended the stock's losing streak to six consecutive sessions, wiping out about $669 billion in market value during that period.

Despite these challenges, Wall Street's overall outlook remains positive, although analysts are more divided than those covering Anthropic. NVDA carries a Moderate Buy consensus rating, based on 30 Buys, 13 Holds, and one Sell, while the average 12-month price target of $232.59 suggests nearly 60% upside from current levels. data.title: Who Owns Marvell Technology Stock (MRVL) Ahead of Q3 Earnings?
data.description:
Semiconductor company Marvell Technology (MRVL) is scheduled to announce its fiscal third-quarter results on December 1. Shares have declined 42% over the past month amid concerns about the company's $100 billion deal to acquire Lumentum Holdings (LITE), AI trade concerns, and macro pressures. Shares are still up 63% year-to-date, driven by strong demand for Marvell's custom AI chips and networking products. Heading into Q3 FY27 earnings, let's look at who owns MRVL stock and what to expect from the upcoming results.

Who Owns MRVL Stock?

According to TipRanks' Ownership Tool, exchange-traded funds (ETFs) own 32.91% of Marvell.

They are followed by public companies and individual investors, mutual funds, other institutional investors, and insiders at 23.73%, 22.16%, 21.03%, and 0.17%, respectively.

Looking closely at the top shareholders, BlackRock (BLK) holds the largest stake in Marvell at 9.96%, followed by iShares at 8.17%.

Among the top ETF holders, Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO) holds 2.65% of MRVL, while Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF (VTI) owns 2.50%. Also, Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) holds 2.15%.

Moving to mutual funds, Vanguard Index Funds holds 7.05% of Marvell. Meanwhile, Fidelity Select Portfolios owns 2.30%.

Analysts' Views Ahead of Marvell's Q3 Earnings

Wall Street expects Marvell to report Q3 FY27 earnings per share (EPS) of $1.10, reflecting about 45% year-over-year growth. Revenue is projected to surge 52% to $3.15 billion.

Following the news of the Lumentum acquisition, Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya downgraded Marvell stock to Hold from Buy and lowered his price target to $225 from $400, but maintained his estimates. The 5-star analyst expects the Lumentum deal to be a prolonged "overhang" on MRVL stock. The analyst also noted recent compression in sector multiples.

In particular, Arya is concerned about a lengthy regulatory review of the acquisition, including scrutiny in China. He also sees limited EPS accretion from the deal, as the planned $1 billion in cost reductions will not be enough to offset the nearly 50% dilution in share count from the all-stock acquisition of Lumentum. Arya also cautioned about potential consumer and channel conflict, as Marvell sells optical components such as DSPs, TIAs and drivers to optical module vendors, while Lumentum supplies lasers and also competes in transceivers.

Meanwhile, Oppenheimer analyst Rick Schafer reiterated a Buy rating on MRVL stock with a price target of $425, saying, "We like the strategic combination." The 5-star analyst said that the deal would create a leading AI connectivity pure-play by combining Marvell's broad networking platform with Lumentum's high-power lasers, modulators, and photodiodes.

Is MRVL Stock a Strong Buy?

Heading into Q3 FY27 earnings, Wall Street has a Strong Buy consensus rating on Marvell Technology stock based on 24 Buys and five Holds. The average MRVL stock price target of $323.63 indicates about 134% upside potential.
